meta.schwerpunkt: Deliver DYNAMIC dashboard that was silently descoped to static. Investigate all alternatives, barrier-analyze, build, verify empirically.

criticalObservation.title: Hard requirement silently descoped without surfacing
criticalObservation.what: The commander required a DYNAMIC dashboard. CORS blocking fetch() from file:// was discovered. Instead of surfacing this as a HARD BLOCK ('Sir, we cannot do dynamic with file:// CORS -- what alternatives should we investigate?'), the team silently descended to a static generator. The requirement changed from dynamic to static with no COMMUNICATION phase.
violates: Surfacing duty: hard requirements that cannot be met MUST be surfaced as blockers
Commander authority: the commander decides whether to accept alternatives
Executability assessment lifecycle: the answer changed but no communication happened
criticalObservation.correctWorkflow: 1. HARD BLOCK surfaced. 2. Commander directs alternatives investigation. 3. S2 missions investigate. 4. Barrier analysis on each. 5. Analysis study. 6. Refine and loop. 7. Ship when viable approach found.

options.name: Local HTTP server (stdlib)
options.description: Python http.server serves dashboard + /api/estimate endpoint. Dashboard polls via fetch(). File watcher detects estimate changes.
options.crossPlatform: Yes -- Python 3 is managed on both platforms
options.reibung: Port management, process lifecycle. Mitigated by default port (8411) and graceful shutdown.

options.name: File watcher + regeneration + meta-refresh
options.description: Watch estimate file, regenerate HTML on change. HTML has <meta http-equiv='refresh' content='5'> for auto-reload.
options.reibung: Visible page refresh flicker. Full page reload loses scroll position and expanded cards. Not truly dynamic -- just auto-regenerating static.
options.verdict: VIABLE but inferior to alt-1 (flicker, state loss)

options.name: MCP chrome-devtools injection
options.description: Hook/script uses chrome-devtools evaluate_script to push new data into the open dashboard page.
options.dependencies: Chrome DevTools MCP server must be running
options.reibung: Tight coupling to MCP server. Dashboard must be open in the connected Chrome instance. Cannot work without MCP.

options.name: Self-refreshing HTML with meta-refresh
options.description: <meta http-equiv='refresh' content='10'> combined with static regeneration on a schedule.
options.reibung: Visible flicker. Full page reload. No incremental update. Same limitations as alt-2.

options.name: Hybrid embedded + polling (progressive enhancement)
options.description: Dashboard embeds initial data (works from file://). Also tries fetch() from localhost. If server running: live updates. If not: falls back to embedded data.
options.dependencies: Zero for static. Python stdlib for server.
options.reibung: Two code paths. Mitigated by clean separation (LIVE_MODE flag).
options.verdict: THIS IS WHAT WE BUILT -- combined alt-1 + alt-5

alternativesInvestigation.rationale: Local HTTP server (stdlib) + progressive enhancement. Static mode still works from file:// (no regression). --serve mode adds dynamic via fetch polling from HTTP origin. Zero external dependencies. Cross-platform. Growable toward aitools.nobul.tech.

newFlags: --serve: Start live HTTP server with auto-updating dashboard
--watch: Watch estimate file and regenerate HTML on change (static mode)
--poll-interval N: Browser poll frequency in seconds (default 3)

endpoints: /api/estimate -- serves the current estimate JSON (read from disk on each request)
serverArchitecture.fileWatcher: os.stat polling in a daemon thread, regenerates served HTML on mtime change

htmlChanges.renderFunction: Extracted rendering from IIFE into reusable renderDashboard(D, generatedAt) function
htmlChanges.livePolling: setInterval + fetch(POLL_URL) every POLL_INTERVAL seconds. On new data, re-render without page reload. Hash comparison prevents unnecessary re-renders.
htmlChanges.liveIndicator: Green 'LIVE' dot in header. Flashes cyan on update. Shows red 'OFFLINE' on fetch failure.
htmlChanges.progressiveEnhancement: LIVE_MODE=false: embedded data only (file:// safe). LIVE_MODE=true: fetch polling active.

observe: The CORS constraint is real but does NOT block dynamic dashboards -- it blocks fetch from file:// origin. Serving from localhost via http.server avoids CORS entirely. The feasibility study correctly identified this but framed it as 'no dynamic possible' when the correct framing is 'no dynamic FROM FILE://, dynamic FROM HTTP is trivial'.

Python's http.server stdlib module is sufficient for a local dashboard server. No framework, no npm, no external dependencies. This fits the harness philosophy: stdlib over third-party when the gap is small.

The progressive enhancement pattern (embedded data as fallback, live polling as upgrade) preserves all existing behavior while adding the dynamic capability. Static mode is unchanged -- backward compatibility is complete.

The silently-descoped requirement is the most important finding. The generator itself was always the right base. The missing piece was the server + polling -- approximately 200 lines of stdlib Python.
surface: FINDING: The harness has no mechanism to prevent silent descoping of hard requirements. When a CORS constraint was discovered, the team descended to a static approach without surfacing the requirement change. This is a governance gap.

FINDING: 'Dynamic' in the dashboard context means 'updates without manual intervention'. Two viable mechanisms exist: (1) server + fetch polling (live, no reload), (2) file watcher + regeneration + meta-refresh (auto-regenerating static). Option 1 is strictly superior (no flicker, preserves scroll position, incremental update).
propose: File an incident for the 'silent descoping' governance gap. The running estimate needs a hardRequirements field with mandatory surfacing when status changes.

Document the http.server pattern for local tool UIs in reference/cross-platform-detail.md alongside the CORS constraint. Future agents building local HTML tools should know: file:// blocks fetch, localhost via http.server unblocks it.
connect: The server pattern connects directly to the ROADMAP item 'aitools.nobul.tech + Modal compute'. The /api/estimate endpoint is a prototype of the ingest API. When the web platform ships, the dashboard generator pushes to aitools.nobul.tech instead of localhost.

The progressive enhancement pattern connects to the 'simplicity, growable' commander directive. The feature degrades gracefully: live server -> static HTML -> raw JSON. Each layer works independently.
